requirements.lead_text: Your Fitness Knowledge and Habits. Do the following with your counselor:
requirements.req_text: Your Fitness Knowledge and Habits. Do the following with your counselor: (a) Explain the physical exercise you regularly do, whether your routine includes all four components of physical fitness (cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition), and how your current practices increase or decrease your likelihood of developing cardiovascular disease or other conditions in adulthood. (b) Discuss what harmful substances you consciously avoid, and how these actions affect your risk factors now and in the future. (c) Explain what common diseases can be prevented or mitigated by vaccinations, and whether you are immunized according to the advice of your healthcare provider and the direction of your parent or guardian. (d) Discuss how good nutrition is related to the other components of personal fitness, and if you follow a nutritious, balanced diet. (e) Discuss what a healthy weight is for you, and what you do to maintain a healthy weight. (f) Explain why getting adequate sleep is important, and whether you get enough hours of sleep each night. (g) Discuss whether you spend quality time with your family and friends in social and recreational activities, and how you contribute to creating and maintaining a good home life.

requirements.lead_text: Measures of Physical Fitness. Determine with your counselor the assessments of physical fitness and nutrition you will do before, during, and after completing the 12-week program in requirement 7.
requirements.req_text: Measures of Physical Fitness. Determine with your counselor the assessments of physical fitness and nutrition you will do before, during, and after completing the 12-week program in requirement 7. (a) Include a measure of cardiorespiratory (aerobic) fitness: Record the time required to complete a mile walk or run as fast as you can. If you are unable to walk or run as a result of a disability that is permanent or is expected to last for longer than two years, work with your counselor to define a test with a similar degree of aerobic challenge. (b) Include two measures of muscular strength and endurance: Record either the number of sit-ups done in 60 seconds OR how long a plank was held; AND, record the number of either push-ups OR pull-ups done in 60 seconds. If you are unable to complete one of these exercises safely and correctly, work with your counselor to replace it with a different exercise that measures strength and endurance. (c) Include at least one measure of flexibility, such as a back-saver sit-and-reach test or a back scratch test.

requirements.req_text: Plan the Program. Outline with your counselor a comprehensive 12-week physical fitness and nutrition program that you will complete based on your improvement goals and ability. The program must incorporate the following: (a) Warm-up: low-intensity movement or gentle muscle stretching before each more rigorous workout (b) Cardiorespiratory (aerobic) element: an activity that raises your heart and respiratory rate for 15 to 30 minutes at least three times per week (c) Muscular strength and endurance element: repetitive exercises that target different muscles, upper body, core, and/or legs, based on your improvement goals and potential (d) Flexibility element: movements that arch/lower/stretch/relax your back, rotate your trunk, or stretch your hamstrings (e) Cool-down: low-intensity movement or gentle stretching to prevent muscle cramps and enhance the benefits of exercise (f) A plan for achieving your two improvement goals related to diet and nutrition

requirements.req_text: Complete the Program. Do the following: (a) Complete and keep a log, over 12 consecutive weeks, of the physical fitness and nutrition program you have outlined. (If your program is interrupted by illness or unavoidable conflicts for less than two weeks, you may resume where you left off, adding the missed days or weeks at the end.) (b) During week 4 and week 8 of your program, repeat the assessments you did in requirement 5(a) before you began. Repeat the same tests for a final assessment within two weeks after completing the 12-week program. Show improvement over your pre-assessment results. (c) For three days during week 8, and again during week 12, keep a log of what you eat and drink. Show improvement toward the diet and nutrition goals you set in requirement 5(d). (d) Discuss your results, improvements, insights, and experiences with your counselor after completing the program and assessments.

pamphlet_excerpts: Exploring Personal Fitness Careers: There are many exciting careers in the field of personal fitness (p. 84).
Personal Trainer Business Policies: Personal trainers should have written policies explaining their services, costs, cancellations, length of contract, and emergency procedures (p. 84).
Exercise Physiologist Evaluations: Exercise physiologists also evaluate cardiovascular and metabolic effects in people, and help active athletes improve and maintain (p. 84).
Workplaces Hiring Fitness Professionals: Colleges and universities, rehabilitation clinics, hospitals, sports and athletic programs, and health/fitness facilities hire exercise physiologists (p. 84).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Evaluate Cardiovascular Exercise Effects: Exercise physiologists also evaluate cardiovascular and metabolic effects in people, and help active athletes improve and maintain (p. 84).

Step 2 - Explore Clinical and Athletic Employers: Colleges and universities, rehabilitation clinics, hospitals, sports and athletic programs, and health/fitness facilities hire exercise physiologists (p. 84).
Step 3 - Maintain First Aid Certifications: They should hold first-aid and CPR certifications (p. 84).
Step 4 - Assist Mobility Through Physical Therapy: People who have trouble moving or performing everyday activities need the help of a physical therapist (p. 84).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before beginning the 12-week Personal Fitness training program, why is a medical physical examination and dental checkup required along with baseline fitness testing?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before beginning the 12-week Personal Fitness training program, why is a medical physical examination and dental checkup required along with baseline fitness testing?
options: A. To exempt Scouts from flexibility and cardiorespiratory testing if they already play a varsity school sport.
B. To calculate maximum one-rep weightlifting loads so you can skip warm-up sets during week one.
C. To replace daily nutrition tracking with a prescription vitamin regimen.
D. To identify any underlying health conditions or physical limitations that need attention before strenuous exercise and to establish safe, individualized health habits.
choices: A. To exempt Scouts from flexibility and cardiorespiratory testing if they already play a varsity school sport.
B. To calculate maximum one-rep weightlifting loads so you can skip warm-up sets during week one.
C. To replace daily nutrition tracking with a prescription vitamin regimen.
D. To identify any underlying health conditions or physical limitations that need attention before strenuous exercise and to establish safe, individualized health habits.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To identify any underlying health conditions or physical limitations that need attention before strenuous exercise and to establish safe, individualized health habits.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): A preventive medical evaluation ensures it is safe to perform vigorous cardiorespiratory and muscular testing and helps tailor the 12-week personal fitness plan to your health needs.

B. Getting a physical examination from your doctor using the Annual Health and Medical Record form
C. Running a timed five-mile race to test your maximum heart rate
D. Eliminating all carbohydrates and fats from your daily meals
choices: A. Purchasing expensive weightlifting shoes and a gym membership
B. Getting a physical examination from your doctor using the Annual Health and Medical Record form

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Getting a physical examination from your doctor using the Annual Health and Medical Record form
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Before starting a personal fitness program, you should get a physical examination from your doctor and document it on the Annual Health and Medical Record form (p. 13).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Which four components must be included to achieve complete physical fitness?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Which four components must be included to achieve complete physical fitness?
options: A. Sprinting speed, vertical jump height, arm size, and calorie counting
B. Weightlifting, marathon running, vitamin supplements, and fasting
C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
D. Morning stretching, sports participation, protein shakes, and hydration
choices: A. Sprinting speed, vertical jump height, arm size, and calorie counting
B. Weightlifting, marathon running, vitamin supplements, and fasting
C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
D. Morning stretching, sports participation, protein shakes, and hydration
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): The four essential components of physical fitness are cardiorespiratory fitness, muscular strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition (p. 45).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why do you compare your initial physical fitness test scores to the percentile tables in the pamphlet?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why do you compare your initial physical fitness test scores to the percentile tables in the pamphlet?
options: A. To see if you are allowed to start the 12-week exercise log
B. To rank Scouts in your troop from most athletic to least athletic
C. To replace the final fitness test at the end of week 12
D. To identify your current fitness baseline and prioritize areas needing improvement
choices: A. To see if you are allowed to start the 12-week exercise log
B. To rank Scouts in your troop from most athletic to least athletic
C. To replace the final fitness test at the end of week 12
D. To identify your current fitness baseline and prioritize areas needing improvement
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To identify your current fitness baseline and prioritize areas needing improvement
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Comparing your assessment scores to the reference tables helps you understand your current fitness level and identify areas at or below the 20th percentile that need extra focus (p. 65).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Before using weights or specialized exercise equipment in your fitness routine, what precaution must you take?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Before using weights or specialized exercise equipment in your fitness routine, what precaution must you take?
options: A. Get instruction on the safe use of the equipment from a qualified coach or instructor
B. Test the heaviest weight available to find your one-repetition maximum
C. Complete at least eight weeks of running before touching any equipment
D. Only use the equipment when you are exercising alone at home
choices: A. Get instruction on the safe use of the equipment from a qualified coach or instructor
B. Test the heaviest weight available to find your one-repetition maximum
C. Complete at least eight weeks of running before touching any equipment
D. Only use the equipment when you are exercising alone at home
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Get instruction on the safe use of the equipment from a qualified coach or instructor
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): To prevent injury, you must never attempt to use weights or special exercise equipment without first getting instruction on safe use from a coach or instructor (p. 74).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: According to the FITT guidelines in the pamphlet, how should you start an aerobic program if you cannot yet jog for 30 minutes continuously?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: According to the FITT guidelines in the pamphlet, how should you start an aerobic program if you cannot yet jog for 30 minutes continuously?
options: A. Push yourself to exhaustion on day one until you finish 30 minutes
B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
C. Skip aerobic exercise completely and only perform sit-ups and push-ups
D. Exercise once every two weeks for two hours at maximum intensity
choices: A. Push yourself to exhaustion on day one until you finish 30 minutes
B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
C. Skip aerobic exercise completely and only perform sit-ups and push-ups
D. Exercise once every two weeks for two hours at maximum intensity
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Alternate periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity and gradually build up to 30 minutes
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): You should start by alternating periods of vigorous and slow or resting activity without exhausting yourself, gradually working up to a 30-minute session (p. 69).

C. Fitness assessments in weeks 4, 8, and after week 12, with three-day diet logs in weeks 8 and 12

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): You repeat your fitness assessments in week 4, week 8, and after completing the program, while keeping three-day nutrition logs during week 8 and week 12 (p. 74).
